from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "The Starting Point: Familiar Euclidean Space"
        lines = [
            "Vectors are often pictured as arrows in space.",
            "We add them by placing them tip-to-tail.",
            "We scale them by stretching or shrinking.",
            "These operations define the geometry of R-squared.",
            "But vectors are much more than just arrows."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        GREEN = "#00FF00"
        BLUE = "#00BFFF"
        PURPLE = "#9B30FF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Create a coordinate system in the grid area
        # Occupying C3-D4 area as the \"center\" of the plane
        plane_center = self.grid["C3"] + (self.grid["D4"] - self.grid["C3"]) / 2
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "tip_width": 0.15, "tip_height": 0.15},
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.4}
        ).move_to(plane_center)
        
        vec_u = Vector([2, 1], color=GREEN)
        vec_u.move_to(plane.c2p(0, 0), aligned_edge=DOWN + LEFT)
        label_u = MathTex(r"\vec{u}", color=GREEN, font_size=24)
        # B038: Avoid axis tips. Place label near the vector tip but offset.
        label_u.next_to(vec_u.get_end(), UR, buff=0.1)

        self.play(Create(plane))
        self.play(GrowArrow(vec_u), Write(label_u))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        vec_v = Vector([1, 2], color=BLUE)
        # Tip-to-tail placement
        vec_v.move_to(plane.c2p(2, 1), aligned_edge=DOWN + LEFT)
        label_v = MathTex(r"\vec{v}", color=BLUE, font_size=24)
        label_v.next_to(vec_v.get_end(), RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        vec_sum = Vector([3, 3], color=PURPLE)
        vec_sum.move_to(plane.c2p(0, 0), aligned_edge=DOWN + LEFT)
        label_sum = MathTex(r"\vec{u} + \vec{v}", color=PURPLE, font_size=24)
        label_sum.next_to(vec_sum.get_end(), UP, buff=0.1)

        # Show addition
        self.play(GrowArrow(vec_v), Write(label_v))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(GrowArrow(vec_sum), Write(label_sum))
        self.wait(1)

        # Cleanup for next step: remove v and sum to focus on u scaling
        self.play(FadeOut(vec_v), FadeOut(label_v), FadeOut(vec_sum), FadeOut(label_sum))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Scaling u by 2
        scaled_u_target = Vector([4, 2], color=GREEN)
        scaled_u_target.move_to(plane.c2p(0, 0), aligned_edge=DOWN + LEFT)
        
        # Using a ValueTracker for smooth scaling animation
        scale_tracker = ValueTracker(1)
        # Update u in place
        vec_u.add_updater(lambda m: m.become(
            Vector(np.array([2, 1, 0]) * scale_tracker.get_value(), color=GREEN).move_to(plane.c2p(0, 0), aligned_edge=DOWN+LEFT)
        ))
        label_u.add_updater(lambda m: m.next_to(vec_u.get_end(), UR, buff=0.1))

        self.play(scale_tracker.animate.set_value(2), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)
        
        vec_u.clear_updaters()
        label_u.clear_updaters()

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Highlight R^2 grid
        plane_highlight = plane.copy().set_stroke(YELLOW, opacity=0.8)
        label_r2 = MathTex(r"\mathbb{R}^2", color=YELLOW, font_size=36)
        # Place label at grid pos A6 (top right corner) - Belief B001/B038 context
        self.place_at_grid(label_r2, "A6")

        self.play(Create(plane_highlight), Write(label_r2))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(plane_highlight))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Preparation for abstraction (fading out the arrow-specific geometry)
        self.play(
            FadeOut(vec_u),
            FadeOut(label_u),
            FadeOut(label_r2),
            plane.animate.set_stroke(opacity=0.1)
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # Reset last line color
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "The 'What If' Moment: Generalization", 
            [
                "Can other objects behave like these arrows?", 
                "Consider functions that we add and scale.", 
                "Vector spaces are broader than we often imagine."
            ]
        )
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Transition from the grid to a black background.
        # We simulate the previous state (grid and arrows) and fade them out.
        sim_plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1], y_range=[-2, 2, 1], 
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.4}
        ).scale(0.5).move_to(self.grid["C3"])
        sim_vector = Arrow(sim_plane.c2p(0,0), sim_plane.c2p(1,1), buff=0, color=YELLOW)
        
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.add(sim_plane, sim_vector)
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(sim_plane), FadeOut(sim_vector), run_time=1)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Icons for a 2x2 matrix, a function curve, and a sequence appear in the center. #F08080
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#F08080")
        
        # 1. 2x2 Matrix
        matrix_mob = MathTex(r"\begin{bmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{bmatrix}", color="#F08080")
        self.place_at_grid(matrix_mob, "B2", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # 2. Function curve (Sine wave)
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[-1, 1, 1], 
            x_length=2, y_length=1.5, 
            axis_config={"include_tip": False, "stroke_width": 2, "color": WHITE}
        )
        sin_graph = axes.plot(lambda x: np.sin(x), color="#F08080")
        function_group = VGroup(axes, sin_graph)
        self.place_at_grid(function_group, "B5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # 3. Sequence
        sequence_mob = MathTex(r"\{a_n\}_{n=1}^\infty = (a_1, a_2, \dots)", color="#F08080")
        # Horizontal extension, use place_in_area per B002
        self.place_in_area(sequence_mob, "D2", "D5", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(
            FadeIn(matrix_mob),
            FadeIn(function_group),
            FadeIn(sequence_mob),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # A white boundary #FFFFFF surrounds the icons, labeled as a 'Vector Space V'.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        icons_group = VGroup(matrix_mob, function_group, sequence_mob)
        boundary = SurroundingRectangle(icons_group, color=WHITE, buff=0.4)
        
        # Label "Vector Space V" centered using place_in_area per B002
        v_label = Text("Vector Space V", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(v_label, "A2", "A5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Create(boundary), run_time=1)
        self.play(Write(v_label), run_time=1)
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard and script
        title = "The 8 Axioms: The 'Membership Rules'"
        lines = [
            "A vector space follows eight strict rules.",
            "These axioms ensure consistent addition and scaling.",
            "Every space must contain a zero element.",
            "Every element must have an additive inverse.",
            "Passing these tests defines a vector space."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_BLUE = "#ADD8E6"
        COLOR_GREEN = "#90EE90"

        # Axiom expressions
        # Belief B002: Use place_in_area for long expressions
        axiom_comm = MathTex("u + v = v + u", color=COLOR_BLUE)
        axiom_assoc = MathTex("(u + v) + w = u + (v + w)", color=COLOR_BLUE)
        axiom_ident = MathTex("v + 0 = v", color=COLOR_BLUE)
        axiom_inv = MathTex("v + (-v) = 0", color=COLOR_BLUE)
        axiom_dist = MathTex("a(u + v) = au + av", color=COLOR_BLUE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "A vector space follows eight strict rules."
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_BLUE))
        self.place_in_area(axiom_comm, "A1", "A3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(axiom_comm))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "These axioms ensure consistent addition and scaling."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_BLUE)
        )
        self.place_in_area(axiom_assoc, "C1", "C3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(axiom_assoc))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "Every space must contain a zero element."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_BLUE)
        )
        self.place_in_area(axiom_ident, "A4", "A6", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(axiom_ident))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # "Every element must have an additive inverse."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(COLOR_BLUE)
        )
        self.place_in_area(axiom_inv, "C4", "C6", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(axiom_inv))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # "Passing these tests defines a vector space."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(COLOR_GREEN)
        )
        
        # Add the distributivity axiom as the final "representative" axiom
        self.place_in_area(axiom_dist, "E1", "E6", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(axiom_dist))
        
        # Flash and turn green
        axioms_group = VGroup(axiom_comm, axiom_assoc, axiom_ident, axiom_inv, axiom_dist)
        self.play(
            Flash(axioms_group, color=COLOR_GREEN, flash_radius=2),
            axioms_group.animate.set_color(COLOR_GREEN)
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Define the content
        title = "Abstract Example: The Space of Polynomials"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Consider the set of all low-degree polynomials.",
            "Adding two polynomials results in another polynomial.",
            "We can even visualize coefficients as coordinates."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        GOLD = "#FFD700"
        CYAN = "#00FFFF"
        ORANGE = "#FFA500"
        WHITE_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Consider the set of all low-degree polynomials.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(GOLD)
        
        poly_p = MathTex("P(x) = ax^2 + bx + c", color=GOLD)
        self.place_in_area(poly_p, "A1", "A6", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(Write(poly_p))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Adding two polynomials results in another polynomial.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE_COLOR)
        
        poly_q = MathTex("Q(x) = dx^2 + ex + f", color=WHITE_COLOR)
        self.place_in_area(poly_q, "B1", "B6", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        poly_sum = MathTex(
            "P(x) + Q(x) = (a+d)x^2 + (b+e)x + (c+f)", 
            color=WHITE_COLOR
        )
        self.place_in_area(poly_sum, "C1", "D6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Write(poly_q))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(Write(poly_sum))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # We can even visualize coefficients as coordinates.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(CYAN)
        
        # Scalar multiplication k*P(x)
        scalar_k = MathTex("k \cdot P(x) = (ka)x^2 + (kb)x + (kc)", color=CYAN)
        self.place_in_area(scalar_k, "E1", "E6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Transform P(x) to show coordinate view
        vector_p = MathTex(r"\text{Coordinates: } \begin{bmatrix} a \\ b \\ c \end{bmatrix}", color=GOLD)
        self.place_in_area(vector_p, "B1", "B6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # "Polynomial Space" label
        label = Text("Polynomial Space", color=ORANGE, font_size=24)
        self.place_in_area(label, "F1", "F6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(
            poly_p.animate.set_color(CYAN),
            FadeOut(poly_q),
            FadeOut(poly_sum),
            Write(scalar_k)
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(poly_p.copy(), vector_p),
            Write(label)
        )
        self.wait(3)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from Storyboard
        title_text = "The Power of Abstraction: Why It Matters"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Abstraction lets us solve many problems at once.",
            "One theorem applies to arrows and functions.",
            "Digital signals are processed as abstract vectors.",
            "This 'Master Key' simplifies complex mathematical systems.",
            "We look past form to see underlying structure."
        ]
        
        # Setup
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        PURPLE = "#DDA0DD"
        WHITE_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"
        YELLOW = "#FFFFE0"
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Abstraction lets us solve many problems at once.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(PURPLE))
        
        # Physics icon: Atom-like
        physics_atom = VGroup(
            Ellipse(width=0.6, height=0.15, color=PURPLE).rotate(PI/3),
            Ellipse(width=0.6, height=0.15, color=PURPLE).rotate(-PI/3),
            Dot(radius=0.05, color=PURPLE)
        )
        physics_label = Text("Physics", font_size=16, color=PURPLE)
        physics_icon = VGroup(physics_atom, physics_label).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        # AI icon: Neural net like
        ai_dots = VGroup(
            Dot(color=PURPLE, radius=0.05).shift(UP*0.2 + LEFT*0.1),

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout with the specific title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout(
            "Summary and Conclusion", 
            [
                "Vectors are elements of any valid vector space.",
                "We moved from arrows to abstract rules.",
                "Linear algebra reveals these universal mathematical patterns."
            ]
        )
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight Line 1
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        # Create a white vector arrow
        arrow = Arrow(start=LEFT, end=RIGHT, color=WHITE)
        # Use place_in_area to span columns B2 to C3 (Belief B001/B002)
        self.place_in_area(arrow, "B2", "C3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Create a white polynomial equation
        poly = MathTex(r"P(x) = a_n x^n + \dots + a_0", color=WHITE)
        # Place in adjacent area B4 to C6
        self.place_in_area(poly, "B4", "C6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Display them side-by-side
        self.play(Create(arrow), Write(poly))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight Line 2
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        
        # Create a green frame labeled '8 Axioms'
        # Group arrow and poly to frame them
        vector_elements = VGroup(arrow, poly)
        frame = SurroundingRectangle(vector_elements, color=GREEN, buff=0.5)
        
        axiom_label = Text("8 Axioms", color=GREEN, font_size=24)
        # Place label below the frame
        self.place_in_area(axiom_label, "D3", "D5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Create(frame), Write(axiom_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight Line 3
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        # Final summary text
        final_text = Text("Abstract Vector Spaces", color=WHITE, font_size=32)
        # Place in a central area of the grid (Belief B002)
        self.place_in_area(final_text, "B2", "D5", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        # Fade out elements from previous steps
        self.play(
            FadeOut(arrow),
            FadeOut(poly),
            FadeOut(frame),
            FadeOut(axiom_label),
            Write(final_text)
        )
        self.wait(3)

outline.topic: Abstract Vector Spaces: Beyond the Arrow

sections.title: The Starting Point: Familiar Euclidean Space
sections.content: Introduce prerequisite knowledge by showing vectors as arrows in a 2D grid (R²). Demonstrate the two fundamental operations: Vector Addition (tip-to-tail) and Scalar Multiplication (stretching/shrinking). Establish that these feel 'natural' because of the visual geometry.
sections.example: An animation of a blue arrow (u) and a red arrow (v) combining to form a purple diagonal (u+v) on a Cartesian plane, then being stretched by a factor of 2.

sections.title: The 'What If' Moment: Generalization
sections.content: Transition from 'arrows' to 'sets of objects'. Challenge the audience to consider if other mathematical objects, like functions or polynomials, could behave like arrows if they follow the same rules of addition and scaling.
sections.example: A 'Magic Box' where you drop in two different sine wave functions. The box adds them together to create a new wave, mirroring how arrows add to create new arrows.

sections.title: The 8 Axioms: The 'Membership Rules'
sections.content: Define an Abstract Vector Space not by what it *is*, but by what it *does*. Present the 8 axioms (Commutativity, Associativity, Identity, etc.) as a checklist. If a set of objects and its operations pass all 8 tests, it is officially a Vector Space.
sections.example: A 'VIP Club' entrance where a 'Polynomial' character approaches a bouncer. The bouncer checks a clipboard (the Axioms). The Polynomial passes because it has a 'Zero' (the number 0) and an 'Inverse' (its negative).

sections.title: Abstract Example: The Space of Polynomials
sections.content: Show a concrete 'abstract' case. Demonstrate that polynomials of degree 'n' form a vector space. Visualize the coefficients as 'coordinates' in a higher-dimensional space, even though they aren't physical directions.
sections.example: A split-screen animation: on the left, adding (2x + 3) and (x + 1); on the right, adding vectors [2, 3] and [1, 1]. Show the visual 'morphing' between the algebraic expression and the geometric coordinate.

sections.title: The Power of Abstraction: Why It Matters
sections.content: Explain that by proving a theorem for 'Abstract Vector Spaces', it automatically applies to arrows, matrices, signals, and functions. This is the 'Master Key' of linear algebra.
sections.example: A digital signal processing scenario: A cat's 'Meow' sound wave being decomposed into simpler frequencies (Basis Vectors). This shows how your phone treats sound as a vector in an abstract space to filter out noise.

sections.title: Summary and Conclusion
sections.content: Summarize the journey: from physical arrows to rule-based sets. Reiterate that a 'Vector' is simply any element of a Vector Space, no matter how strange it looks.
sections.example: A final graphic showing a 'Vector Tree' where the roots are the Axioms, the trunk is the 'Abstract Vector Space', and the branches are diverse fields like Quantum Mechanics, Computer Graphics, and Statistics.

storyboard.title: The Starting Point: Familiar Euclidean Space
lecture_lines: Vectors are often pictured as arrows in space.
We add them by placing them tip-to-tail.
We scale them by stretching or shrinking.
These operations define the geometry of R-squared.
But vectors are much more than just arrows.
animations: A 2D coordinate grid appears with a green vector [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/arrow.svg] #00FF00 starting at the origin.
A blue vector [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/arrow.svg] #00BFFF is added to the first, showing the parallelogram addition rule.
The green vector [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/arrow.svg] scales to double its length to demonstrate scalar multiplication.

storyboard.title: The 'What If' Moment: Generalization
lecture_lines: Can other objects behave like these arrows?
Consider functions that we add and scale.
Vector spaces are broader than we often imagine.
animations: The 2D grid and arrows fade out to a black background.

Icons for a 2x2 matrix [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/matrix.svg], a function curve [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/curve.svg], and a sequence appear in the center. #F08080
A white boundary #FFFFFF surrounds the icons, labeled as a 'Vector Space V'.

storyboard.title: The 8 Axioms: The 'Membership Rules'
lecture_lines: A vector space follows eight strict rules.
These axioms ensure consistent addition and scaling.
Every space must contain a zero element.
Every element must have an additive inverse.
Passing these tests defines a vector space.
animations: The Commutativity axiom 'u + v = v + u' appears in light blue #ADD8E6 at the top.
The Associativity axiom '(u + v) + w = u + (v + w)' appears below it.
The Additive Identity axiom 'v + 0 = v' appears on the right side.
The Distributive property 'a(u + v) = au + av' appears below the identity.
All displayed axioms flash and turn light green #90EE90 to show they define the space.

storyboard.title: Abstract Example: The Space of Polynomials
lecture_lines: Consider the set of all low-degree polynomials.
Adding two polynomials results in another polynomial.
We can even visualize coefficients as coordinates.
animations: A polynomial 'P(x) = ax^2 + bx + c' appears in gold #FFD700.
A second polynomial 'Q(x) = dx^2 + ex + f' appears below it.
The coefficients of P and Q group together to show how polynomials add like vectors.
A scalar 'k' multiplies each term of P(x), changing its color to cyan #00FFFF.
A label 'Polynomial Space' appears at the bottom in orange #FFA500.

storyboard.title: The Power of Abstraction: Why It Matters
lecture_lines: Abstraction lets us solve many problems at once.
One theorem applies to arrows and functions.
Digital signals are processed as abstract vectors.
This 'Master Key' simplifies complex mathematical systems.
We look past form to see underlying structure.
animations: Three icons representing 'Physics', 'AI', and 'Signals' appear in purple #DDA0DD.
Arrows from each icon point toward a central 'Vector Space' circle. #FFFFFF
The central circle pulses with a pale yellow light #FFFFE0 to signify universal application.

storyboard.title: Summary and Conclusion
lecture_lines: Vectors are elements of any valid vector space.
We moved from arrows to abstract rules.
Linear algebra reveals these universal mathematical patterns.
animations: A vector arrow and a polynomial equation appear side-by-side in white #FFFFFF.
A green frame #00FF00 labeled '8 Axioms' wraps around both objects.
All elements fade out, leaving the final title 'Abstract Vector Spaces' in white.
